newsitem.title: INDIA: India rupee zigzags as leading bank buys and sells.
newsitem.headline: India rupee zigzags as leading bank buys and sells.

text.p: The Indian rupee moved both ways against the dollar on Thursday, reacting to buy and sell orders of a leading state-run bank, dealers said.
The rupee opened at 35.80/82 per dollar and briefly dipped below the 35.80 mark when the state-run bank struck, pulling the rupee to the day's low of 35.840.
The bank mopped up dollars just as it did on Wednesday, when its dollar buying spree sent the rupee to 35.81 from 35.73 opening, dealers said.
The same bank sold dollars on Thursday afternoon, leading to the rupee's recovery to 35.78/79 levels.
"They sensed the market was long," said a dealer at a foreign bank in Bombay. "So they decided to cool off."
"Below 35.80 level, they were again buying," he said.
Most dealers said the the bank appeared to be buying for a state-run oil company to pay for India's rising oil imports.
Nor do dealers expect the rupee to appreciate further even if the spurt in dollar demand cools off.
"I would expect RBI (the Reserve Bank of India) to buy even at these levels," said a dealer. The RBI has been buying dollars at 35.73 levels in recent weeks, he said.
Some dealers said it was only a matter of months before the rupee touched the 36 per dollar mark.
The rupee weakened on the forward market too but this was largely a reflection of rise in call rates, dealers said.
Six month annualised premia was quoted at 8.05 percent compared to the previoius close of 7.32 percent, they said.
